title.title: Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa and Nakayama conjectures fail
title.subtitle: Claim: over $k = \mathbb{F}_2(q,H_1,H_2)$, rigid non-projective modules break a whole family of conjectures

plain: Several old rules said 'a module with no self-twists is trivial'; one example breaks them all

beats.text: All these conjectures say a module with no self-extensions is projective
Two base counterexamples, both in Lean: a non-projective module with all Ext groups zero
The step from them to Nakayama and the rest is on paper only

steps: Build a symmetric algebra with a rigid module that is not projective
That already breaks Tachikawa and Auslander–Reiten
Its endomorphism algebra then breaks Nakayama's conjecture

achievement.label: Auslander–Reiten (1975), Tachikawa (1973), Nakayama (1958)
achievement.context: Counterexample: finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb{F}_2(q,H_1,H_2)$, stable under field extension

verify.detail: Both base counterexamples are in Lean; the step to Nakayama and the rest is paper-only
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean scope notes; we did not run the checker

voice.text: These conjectures all say a module with no self-extensions must be projective.
A symmetric algebra with a rigid module; its endomorphism algebra then breaks Nakayama too.
Claimed: counterexamples over a field of characteristic two.

sources.quote: Auslander–Reiten (1975): a module $M$ with $\operatorname{Ext}^i(M,M\oplus A)=0$ for all $i>0$ is projective.
Both base counterexamples are in Lean
The step to Nakayama and the rest is paper-only, and so is everything outside characteristic 2.
all persist under every field extension
